thread:
emma: Quick thread to finalize the 'Burst Guard' packaging model. Two enterprise pilots asked for a burst top-up that sits above their committed slab. Need final gating rules and how it appears on invoices.
yusuf: Option A = auto-burst: tenant can exceed slab; we bill at higher overage rate. Option B = purchased burst credits that draw down before overage kicks in.
claire: Customer preference: credits model (Option B) because it's predictable. They want price per 100k tokens and a daily cap.
ben: Engineering constraints: credits are simplest for accounting but require a drawdown/expiry policy and reconciliation. Auto-burst is easier on infra but messier for predictability.
emma: Proposal: pilot with 'Burst Credits' SKU (BURST-C1). Credits sold in blocks (100k tokens/unit). Credits expire monthly unless converted to rollover in annual plans.
sales-bot: Draft SKU: BURST-C1 price = $200 per 100k tokens. Annual rollover option = +15% premium, converts to non-expiring annual bucket.
yusuf: Enforcement: credits consumed first, then slab, then overage. Wait, that ordering might surprise customers; maybe slab should be consumed first.
claire: Customers expect commitments to be used first. So ordering should be slab -> credits -> overage. Credits used only after commitment depleted.
ben: Implementation detail: meter stores counters per tenant: committed_consumed, credits_consumed, overage_consumed. Example billing_key schema:
```
billing_key = f"tenant:{tid}:month:{yyyymm}"
fields = ["committed", "credits", "overage"]
```
ops-bot: Guardrail: if overage > 20% of committed usage in 24h, generate auto-alert + a rate-limit escalation until approval.
emma: Launch gating checklist suggestion: - two pilot customers buy BURST-C1 - invoice samples show correct line ordering - expiry/rollover logic validated - messaging + support FAQ ready
yusuf: Pricing tweak: make first 100k credit block discounted 10% for pilots to encourage trial.
claire: We also need clear contract language: how rollover works, refund policy on unused credits (no refunds except for annual rollover conversion), and transferability rules.
ben: Edgecase: if customer purchases credits mid-month, pro-rate? Simpler: full block price regardless of purchase date for pilot.
sales-bot: I'll add SKU to ratecard: BURST-C1 and create sample invoice line: "Burst Credits (100k) xN - BURST-C1" with metadata: tag=burst, exp=YYYY-MM.
emma: Decision (tentative): ship Burst Credits pilot (BURST-C1) with slab-first consumption order, monthly expiry by default, optional annual rollover. Pilot pricing: $180/100k first block for pilots, $200 thereafter. Guardrail: overage alert at 20%+ per day.
yusuf: Next actions: @ben implement meter changes (ETA 2w), @claire draft contract & faq (ETA 3d), @sales-bot seed pilot offers and collect signups (ETA 1w).
claire: I'll include sample contract clause: "Burst credits are non-refundable and expire at month end unless converted under annual rollover." Will circulate for legal review.
emma: Great. I'll post a one-pager to product docs and add acceptance criteria to the pilot tracker. Thanks everyone :rocket:
